speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what safeguards are in place to protect members of the public, particularly children and women, from recalcitrant sex offenders; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider lifelong counselling and monitoring of these offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members know that the law provides for stiff action to be taken and stiff action is taken against sex offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These include longer imprisonment terms and sentences under the Corrective Training (CT) and Preventive Detention (PD) regimes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Under both CT and PD regimes, repeat offenders can be sentenced to imprisonment terms which are longer than the maximum term prescribed for the offence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Such offenders also undergo longer rehabilitation programmes and supervision.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members know that we have been extremely focused on this proactively, always looking to see what else we can do to try and protect members of the public, particularly vulnerable members of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I had asked the Minstry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) to study a new sentencing option, quite a novel approach, to give more protection to the public from dangerous first-time offenders as well as repeat offenders, who commit very serious hurt and sexual offences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When the jail sentences end, when they have completed it, there will be no automatic release.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At the point of release, they have to be assessed as to whether they pose a threat to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If they are assessed to continue to pose a threat, they will continue to be detained.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This, as Members can see, would represent a major change in the way our sentencing regime works, because, today, the Court imposes a sentence and when it ends, the person is released.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The UK tried this approach, I have to say, with very mixed results.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But I think we can make it work, and the rationale is very simple.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is a serious heinous offence, say, raping a young child or a rape followed by murder.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The judge can express outrage, he can impose a very stiff sentence, assuming it is not capital punishment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But the judge will not know whether, in X number of years, the person will no longer remain a danger to society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And there have been enough cases around the world where the day after the person is released, literally, he goes out and commits another serious offence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have had not many, but we have had one or two cases in Singapore, too.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Obviously, we will come back to the House because any such approach is going to require changes to the law.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In addition to the above, agencies like the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) work closely with the Police to screen those who apply for jobs when they have to work with children in licensed preschools and schools.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Member suggested that MHA consider lifelong counselling and monitoring of recalcitrant sex offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Today, a sex offender is given psychological assistance by the Singapore Prison Service's (SPS) psychologists.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Those who have committed serious sexual offences can also be put on the Mandatory Aftercare Scheme (MAS).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: SPS also works closely with the families of ex-offenders and community partners to support them after their release.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will refer the Member's suggestion to consider lifelong counselling and monitoring for recalcitrant sex offenders to the relevant agencies for them to consider.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The safeguards are in licensed vocations, regulated industries or institutions – I mentioned MOE-registered kindergartens and schools.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, employees at these licensed childhood centres, regulated by MSF or Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), must be screened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But those who work in enrichment centres or other commercial service providers for children do not need to be screened in today's framework.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Even then, in licensed premises, the question is whether all employees need to be screened, for example, cleaners and so on.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We know that MOE does a screening for all, including cleaners, but others may not.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have asked my Ministries to look into the screening framework to see how the process can be strengthened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we need to have a balance between making sure that people have a second chance, but, at the same time, protecting the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are some not so easy issues to consider; for example, what about freelance providers of services – piano teachers or swimming coaches?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, the regulatory framework for that is not so easy to consider, but we will look at it and we will come back before the House.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand this is a review that is in progress and full details of the proposals are not before the House.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The first question, as I understand it, is whether we are assessing the current detainees, people who are in jail, for their re-integration back into society.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in order to do rehabilitation, when someone who has been imposed with a custodial sentence comes into prison, he or she is assessed on a certain matrix of factors to see what sort of intervention is necessary to help the person.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Without going into too much detail, they may be classified as low-risk, medium-risk or high-risk, for example.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And depending on the total set of factors, including the risk within prison and outside, they are given tailored interventions and assistance, job training, education – you name it – different things.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Of course, some, based on our assessment, are not suitable for immediate job training, for example.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They need other sorts of intervention first, to get them to be in a place where they can be better rehabilitated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there are a whole series of factors and approaches, and it is done through the period of detention.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But, of course, if they are in there for three months or six months, then these approaches do not work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We are talking about detainees or people in jail for a longer period of time and assessed to be in need of such assistance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, when they come out, we no longer take the approach that "you are out and, therefore, you are no longer my obligation".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not saying that it works for every releasee.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some do not want to know us and, obviously, this only works on the basis of consent.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But for those who need assistance – and, again, we do not have the full set of resources to assist everyone – we try and do our best for as many as we can.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I think I am answering the question that was asked.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Leader of the Opposition can file a separate question on that, if he wishes.
